newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia says will meet 800,000 T wheat target.
newsitem.headline: Croatia says will meet 800,000 T wheat target.

text.p: Croatia expects to meet its 800,000-tonne target for 1997 wheat output, the government said on Monday following claims that wet weather had delayed the harvest and damaged wheat and maize crops.
"Croatia will this summer harvest 820,000 tonnes of wheat, which should suffice for domestic consumption," Croatian news agency HINA quoted Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic as saying.
"Harvesting has begun and first data show the wheat crop has exceeded our expectations," he said.
He said a ban on wheat and flour exports would be extended until the end of September.
Analysts last week raised doubts about the government-set harvest target, saying wheat was not being harvested due to the wet spell that started 10 days ago.
"There will be some serious losses due to washing out and deterioration in the quality of the grain," an analyst with the Croatian grain producers' association told Reuters last week.
Farmers planted some 250,000 hectares of wheat last autumn, 30 percent more than a year earlier.
But only 15 percent of the crop has been harvested so far in the largest grain area around Osijek in Eastern Slavonia.
